user.title: Connect to Norman Hub
user.description: Connect to your Norman Hub to control your blinds. The hub is reached directly on your local network; nothing goes through the cloud.

data_description.host: The address of the Norman Hub on your network. Give it a fixed address in your router so it does not change.

zeroconf_confirm.title: Norman Hub found
zeroconf_confirm.description: Add the Norman Hub at {host}? It was found on your local network and answered as a Norman hub.

reconfigure.title: Update Norman Hub address
reconfigure.description: Enter the hub's new address. It must be the same hub this entry was set up with.

data_description.host: The address of the Norman Hub on your network.

data.show_sidebar_panel: Show Norman Shades in the sidebar

data_description.control_interval: Seconds to leave between commands sent to the hub. The hub has one radio and silently drops commands that arrive faster than it can transmit them, so a scene covering several blinds is queued and sent one at a time. Raise this if some blinds still miss a command they were sent alongside others; lower it to make large scenes finish sooner. The default is 1.6 seconds.
data_description.show_sidebar_panel: Show Norman Shades, every blind by room, in the Home Assistant sidebar. With more than one hub, each gets its own entry. Turn off to remove it; Norman Shades can still be added to a dashboard as a card.
data_description.sidebar_view: What the windows on the Norman Shades page in the sidebar look out on: a photograph chosen by the time of day and the weather. A room's windows share one view, and the page behind takes its colors. Choose the Big Sur coast or Lake Tahoe, or None for the plain page. The photographs are CC0 or in the public domain ([photo credits]({credits})).
data_description.sidebar_view_motion: Sets the photograph moving: its clouds and water drift, rain and snow fall, stars twinkle, and birds, a moon and shooting stars cross the sky. Turn off to show it still. It is also shown still on a device set to reduce motion.
data_description.sidebar_view_forecast: Shows the weather at the top of the Norman Shades page: the temperature, the conditions and the forecast, the hours ahead with each one's weather, temperature and chance of rain or snow, or the days ahead from a weather entity that forecasts only by the day. Turn off to leave the weather out; the page still shows how many shades are open. With the view set to None the page shows no weather at all.
data_description.sidebar_view_weather: The weather entity the view follows, and whose temperature, conditions and forecast the page shows. Leave empty to use Home Assistant's own forecast, or the first weather entity there is.

error.control_interval_out_of_range: Enter a value between 0.3 and 5 seconds.

nudge_position.name: Nudge position
nudge_position.description: Move a cover by a relative amount from where it is heading (or is).

step.name: Step
step.description: Amount to move by, -100 to 100. Positive opens, negative closes.

nudge_tilt.name: Nudge tilt
nudge_tilt.description: Adjust a cover's tilt by a relative amount from where it is heading (or is).

step.name: Step
step.description: Amount to tilt by, -100 to 100. Positive opens: it raises a two-rail blind's middle rail and opens a SmartDrape's vanes or a Shutter's louvers, by at least one stop for any step.

room_command.name: Room command
room_command.description: Run one of the Norman app's room buttons against a room, chosen blinds, or every blind. best_privacy, best_view, favorite and stop go to a room in a single request; refresh sends a status request to each blind.

room.name: Room
room.description: The room's name as the hub knows it (the Norman app's room name). Leave this and Blinds empty to address every blind on the hub.

blinds.name: Blinds
blinds.description: Instead of a room, these blinds and no others, whatever area they are in. A whole room among them still gets a single request.

command.name: Command
command.description: best_privacy closes the bottom rail and fully opens the middle rail; best_view fully opens both rails; favorite sends the blinds to their stored favorite; refresh asks each blind to report in (nothing moves); stop stops every blind where it is.

config_entry_id.name: Hub
config_entry_id.description: Which hub, when more than one is set up.

get_hub_data.name: Get hub data
get_hub_data.description: Read the hub's raw device list and status, every field included. Returns a response; use it from Developer Tools or a script when reporting an unsupported blind. The hub's identity is blanked, and blinds are called blind_1, blind_2 and so on instead of by serial number.

config_entry_id.name: Hub
config_entry_id.description: Which Norman hub to read. Optional when only one is configured.

show_serial_numbers.name: Show serial numbers
show_serial_numbers.description: Give each blind's real id, its serial number, instead of blind_1, blind_2 and so on. Leave off for a response you will post in an issue.

send_hub_command.name: Send hub command
send_hub_command.description: Advanced. POST arbitrary fields to the hub's control endpoint for one blind and return the reply. For the hub verbs that have no entity of their own, such as setting or clearing a limit. The blind will do whatever the hub makes of the fields.

config_entry_id.name: Hub
config_entry_id.description: Which Norman hub to send to. Optional when only one is configured.

peripheral_uid.name: Peripheral UID
peripheral_uid.description: The blind's id, the serial number on its device page. It is also the cover's unique id.

fields.name: Fields
fields.description: Extra JSON fields for the control call. PeripheralUID, Timestamp and TaskID are filled in automatically.
